incumbent.name: Tim O'Brien
incumbent.summary: Tim O'Brien, an Evansville Republican and real estate broker, has represented House District 78 since 2021, when a Republican caucus chose him to fill the seat Holli Sullivan left on becoming Secretary of State {caucus_obrien} {news14_sworn}. He chairs the House Ways and Means K-12 subcommittee {caucus_obrien}.
record: Serves on Government and Regulatory Reform, Ways and Means (chair of its K-12 subcommittee) and Veterans Affairs and Public Safety, per the House Republican caucus {caucus_obrien}.

April 10, 2025: Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (passed 65-29) {rc_sea1_433}. April 25, 2025: Voted yes on the 2025 budget (HEA 1001), adopted 66-27 {rc_hb1001_576}. Dec. 5, 2025: Voted yes on HB 1032, the mid-decade congressional redistricting bill, which passed the House 57-41 {rc_hb1032_28}.
Jan. 28, 2026: Voted yes on HB 1002, the 2026 electric utility affordability bill (passed 89-4) {rc_hb1002_149}.

2026 session: Authored HEA 1250, requiring the Department of Correction to give victims and local police seven days' electronic notice before a serious violent felon's release; co-authored HEA 1001, the House Republican housing bill that limits local regulations the caucus says raise home prices {caucus_session2026}.

Laws the caucus lists as his include a 2022 requirement that school boards allow public comment, 2023 protection of firefighters' personal information online, and 2025 laws creating an Indiana-Ireland trade commission and pediatric and breast cancer research grants {caucus_obrien}.

Critique: Challenger Sally Busby's campaign says O'Brien voted against eleven consumer-protection amendments to HB 1002 and links his campaign contributions from real estate and utility PACs to his legislation {busby_site} {busby_accountability}. No response from O'Brien was found.

race_context: House District 78 covers parts of Vanderburgh and Warrick counties in southwestern Indiana {caucus_obrien}; Busby describes campaigning from McCutchanville to Newburgh {busby_site}.
O'Brien was reelected without opposition in 2024 {wiki_2026}. Both O'Brien and Sally Busby were unopposed for their parties' nominations in the May 5, 2026 primary {wiki_2026}.

Forums: The Evansville NAACP and League of Women Voters of Southwestern Indiana invited all local and state candidates on the ballot to a Sept. 12, 2026 forum in Evansville {wnin_forum}; which candidates attended was not reported. No head-to-head debate was found.

Key differences: Busby centers her campaign on utility rate caps and public school funding instead of vouchers {busby_priorities}; O'Brien cites state investments in education, housing supply and child care {news_obrien_rerun} {caucus_session2026}.

candidates.summary: Sally Busby is an assistant professor in the University of Evansville School of Education and a former middle school teacher, making her first run for office {evpl_guide} {busby_meet}. She focuses on utility bills and public school funding {busby_site}.
background: Assistant professor at the University of Evansville School of Education; previously taught middle school for fifteen years; holds a doctorate in literacy research {evpl_guide} {busby_meet}.
Active in Rotary, Bridge, the NAACP and the League of Women Voters; has not held elected office {evpl_guide}. Lives in District 78 {busby_meet}.
path_to_ballot: Filed Feb. 3, 2026 at the Vanderburgh County elections office {wnin_filing}; unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary {wiki_2026}.

items: Supports "real rate caps and accountability" for utilities such as CenterPoint, statutory caps on single-year rate hikes, outage compensation, repeal of the SB 271 carve-out and legalizing community solar and wind micro-grids {busby_priorities}.
Says she opposes rate increases beyond what the state Office of Utility Consumer Counselor found justified {busby_site}.

"Fully fund public schools instead of draining them to pay for vouchers"; supports smaller classes and support for students who learn differently {busby_priorities}. Says voucher funding "should follow a kid into a classroom that has to take them" {busby_site}.
Seeks to "Protect and expand access to affordable healthcare for working families" and support families caring for relatives with disabilities {busby_priorities}.
Supports protections against "unfair rent hikes and surprise fees" and accountability for landlords who do not maintain safe homes {busby_priorities}.
Supports apprenticeship pathways, collective bargaining rights and investment in the trades and health care workforce {busby_priorities}.

on_incumbent: Says her opponent "voted no on every single one" of eleven consumer-protection amendments to HB 1002 and that she "will vote yes" {busby_site}.

Her campaign's accountability page lists real estate, builder and utility PAC contributions to O'Brien and criticizes housing, utility and education bills he co-authored or supported, including HB 1001 (2026) and HB 1136 {busby_accountability}.
plans: Says she holds regular town halls and wants a representative who is present year-round {busby_meet}. Says she is not taking corporate PAC money {busby_site}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements listed on her campaign site; she says she is not accepting corporate PAC money {busby_site}. No campaign finance totals found.
gaps: No position found on the 2025 property-tax law (SEA 1), data centers or redistricting.
A podcast episode (seen in search results only) discusses her reasons for running; not reviewed.
Her campaign's figures for projected utility bill savings are campaign estimates and were not verified.

candidates.summary: Tim O'Brien is a realtor who has represented District 78 since 2021 and chairs the Ways and Means K-12 subcommittee {caucus_obrien} {evpl_guide}. He cites investments in education, housing and child care in seeking reelection {news_obrien_rerun} {caucus_session2026}.
background: Real estate broker; economics graduate of the University of Southern Indiana (2015); in 2019 became the youngest president of the Southwest Indiana Association of Realtors {caucus_obrien}.

Chairs the Heritage Federal Credit Union board and has served on the Evansville Land Bank board; named 2025 Easterseals Evansville Legislator of the Year and a 2025 Boys & Girls Clubs of Indiana Legislative Champion {caucus_obrien} {evpl_guide}. Lives in Evansville {caucus_obrien}.
path_to_ballot: Unopposed in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary {wiki_2026}.

items: On HEA 1001: "These new laws will help expand housing supply" {caucus_session2026}. Co-authored a 2026 bill limiting HOA fee increases and protecting home-based child care {caucus_obrien}.
Authored the 2026 law on advance notice to victims and police before a serious violent felon's release {caucus_session2026}.
Points to "historic investments in education" as an accomplishment {news_obrien_rerun}.
Co-sponsored SEA 4, allowing state reserve money to fund the Child Care and Development Fund voucher program {caucus_session2026}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. Said serving the district is "an honor I never take for granted" and "there's more to do" {news_obrien_rerun}. No statements about Busby were found.
plans: Says "Hoosiers deserve leaders who stay focused on real-world results" {news_obrien_rerun}.
endorsements_finance: No 2026 endorsements or campaign finance totals were found; Busby's campaign lists contributions it says he received from real estate, utility and other PACs in 2022–2026 {busby_accountability}.
gaps: Campaign website has no issue pages.
No statement found from O'Brien on utility rates, data centers, the 2025 property-tax law or his redistricting vote.
Campaign finance totals not independently checked.
Busby's specific claims (eleven HB 1002 amendment votes, PAC totals, HB 1136 school-district provisions, SB 271/HB 1209) were not verified against roll calls or filings.
The WEHT reelection story's exact publication date was not shown.
